more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Fumaric acid is the trans form of an unsaturated dicarboxylic acid used to regulate acidity. Its acidity-regulating role is to adjust or maintain the pH of the food. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material. EU permissions include flavoured drinks, flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products, other confectionery including breath freshening micro-sweets, chewing gum.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; desserts excluding products covered in categories 1, 3 and 4.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: For fumaric acid: No ADI specified (JECFA, 1999). This evaluation does not establish an ADI for every form in the named group.
